grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Time clauses with as soon as
grammarPoints.rule: Use as soon as to say that the second thing happened immediately after the first. Both verbs are in the simple past when you talk about the past.
grammarPoints.pattern: As soon as + past clause, + past clause

chart.title: Time clauses with as soon as

intro_examples.text: As soon as the Santa Margarita sank, people began looking for the silver.
intro_examples.jp: サンタ・マルガリータ号が沈むとすぐ、人々は銀を探し始めました。

intro_examples.text: Water poured into the Titanic as soon as it hit the iceberg.
intro_examples.jp: タイタニック号は氷山に衝突するとすぐ、水が流れ込みました。

intro_examples.text: As soon as the two ships crashed, an enormous fire started.
intro_examples.jp: 2隻の船が衝突するとすぐ、巨大な火事が起こりました。

rows.pattern: As soon as + past clause, + past clause
rows.example: As soon as the Santa Margarita sank, people began looking for the silver.
rows.jp: サンタ・マルガリータ号が沈むとすぐ、人々は銀を探し始めました。

rows.pattern: past clause + as soon as + past clause
rows.example: Water poured into the Titanic as soon as it hit the iceberg.
rows.jp: タイタニック号は氷山に衝突するとすぐ、水が流れ込みました。

rows.pattern: comma only when as soon as comes first
rows.example: As soon as the two ships crashed, an enormous fire started.
rows.jp: as soon as が先に来るときだけコンマを打ちます。

rows.example: As soon as I am captain, I'll find your treasure.
rows.jp: 船長になったらすぐ、おまえの宝を見つけよう。

rows.pattern: the as soon as clause happens first
rows.example: As soon as it hit the iceberg, water poured in.
rows.jp: as soon as の節のできごとが先に起こります。

chart.note_rule: As soon as always marks the earlier event, wherever it appears in the sentence.
chart.note_exception: When you talk about the future, use the present tense after as soon as, not will.
chart.note_exception_detail: Put a comma after the as soon as clause only when it starts the sentence.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: It's + adjective + infinitive
grammarPoints.rule: Use It's or It isn't + an adjective + to + the base verb to judge an action — to say it is important, useful, safe, legal or not.
grammarPoints.pattern: It's / It isn't + adjective + to + base verb

chart.note_rule: The it at the front does not mean anything on its own — it points forward to the to-phrase.
chart.note_exception: You can say the same thing with the opposite adjective: It isn't legal = It's illegal.
chart.note_exception_detail: The verb after to is always the base form: to know, to take, to be.

tab4_master.jp: to のあとは原形です。

japanese.title: It's + 形容詞 + to不定詞
japanese.rule: It's / It isn't + 形容詞 + to + 動詞の原形 で、その行動が大切か、役に立つか、安全か、合法かを判断して言います。
japanese.pattern: It's / It isn't + 形容詞 + to + 動詞の原形

examples.sentence: It's important to know how to swim.
examples.highlight: It's important to know

examples.sentence: It's useful to know how to swim.
examples.highlight: It's useful to know

examples.sentence: It's necessary to know how to swim.
examples.highlight: It's necessary to know

examples.sentence: It's helpful to know how to swim.
examples.highlight: It's helpful to know

examples.sentence: It isn't legal to take artifacts from this shipwreck.

examples.sentence: It isn't safe to take artifacts from this shipwreck.
examples.highlight: It isn't safe to take

examples.sentence: It isn't right to take artifacts from this shipwreck.
examples.highlight: It isn't right to take

examples.sentence: It's illegal to be a pirate.
